title: Data science homework 1
text:
data science is about turning data into actionable insights.
data science has a much heavier coding aspect, statisticians also tend to have more theoretical training while I have always seen data science as much more applied. I do think that recently the line between the two has been getting more and more faded.
I have always been more of a data scientist in my internships and during school


y <- density(iris$Petal.Width)
class(y)

[1] "density"

typeof(y)

[1] "list"

str(y)

List of 8
 $ x         : num [1:512] -0.656 -0.648 -0.64 -0.633 -0.625 ...
 $ y         : num [1:512] 0.00161 0.00178 0.00197 0.00217 0.00239 ...
 $ bw        : num 0.252
 $ n         : int 150
 $ old.coords: logi FALSE
 $ call      : language density.default(x = iris$Petal.Width)
 $ data.name : chr "iris$Petal.Width"
 $ has.na    : logi FALSE
 - attr(*, "class")= chr "density"


Here is are some of the attributes of the data, y is of class ‘density’ and is stored as a list, it has the name “width” and N=150undefined









Here is a plot of density vs the width on the 150 trials, using plot(y)
